body.statement: Can the partial-trace handle be completed into a bounded finite-production grammar \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{FS}}\) such that every residual failure contains a forest-supported local response obstruction that extends to two models \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) satisfying \(P_{M_1}(V)=P_{M_2}(V)\), \(\operatorname{supp}_V(M_1)=\operatorname{supp}_V(M_2)\), and witness-dependent target separation \(\Delta=|q(M_1)-q(M_2)|>0\), while preserving the supplied observed alphabets \(\Omega\) and the latent-source architecture of \(G\): each \(M_j\) uses exactly the roots \(U\) with the parent incidences of \(G\), may use finite model-specific latent alphabets bounded by \(H(L)\), and separately satisfies \(P_{M_j}(U)=\prod_{u\in U}P_{M_j}(u)\), without requiring \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) to share root masses? Can absence of an obstruction reconstruct a support-valid guarded formula, and can exhaustive search of the grammar terminate within an explicit bound and return exactly one terminal certificate on every input: a support contradiction when \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)=\varnothing\), and otherwise either a guarded formula derivation or a NONID certificate? The grammar must specify the finite syntax of each terminal certificate. Conditional on that completed syntax and rule set, it must make rule recognition decidable: support contradictions are checked by finite support enumeration; guarded derivations are checked production by production with every positivity guard and compiled to an observable expression; and NONID certificates are checked by exact rational arithmetic for normalization, graph and functional-row compatibility, satisfaction of \(\Pi\), equality of all observed cells and exact support, unequal targets, preservation of the latent-source architecture, and the encoding bounds in \(\mathrm{def:rational-certificate-encoding}\). The result must derive explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\), an explicit search-state bound in \(L\), and explicit computable bit-operation and output-size bounds in \(L\) and \(\ell(C)\) for checking a supplied terminal certificate. It must resolve \(\mathcal B_0\), strictly extend ordinary hedge completeness, go beyond Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions, and admit declared support faces outside the Theorem 18 treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). It must also strictly cover the residual regime outside Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2: arbitrary declared zero-and-positive event literals and qualitative functional nodes, rather than only their sound identification under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law. For each existentially constructed rational witness pair, every rational pair must use the primitive, individual-denominator encoding of \(\mathrm{def:rational-certificate-encoding}\), including its displayed induced-cell and total serialized bit-size bounds; no instance-uniform lower bound on \(\Delta\) is asserted.
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it must replace classical parity softening by an exact support-preserving lift that retains the latent-source architecture of \(G\).
body.gap: Shpitser and Pearl construct unrestricted binary hedge pairs. Chen and Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions, whereas Theorem 18 assumes \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem takes arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support literals as input. Chen and Darwiche's constrained-identifiability work gives arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests, including logical and \(0\)--\(1\) constraints, but not a complete procedure for this arbitrary support-literal and functional class or an exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy. Chen and Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 prove soundness of formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints, under a strictly positive observational law; they neither prove completeness under those constraints nor admit an input that keeps a treatment state in \(\Omega\) while declaring its observational probability zero. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash give a sound-and-complete gID algorithm under a positive observational law, but do not handle arbitrary declared support faces or supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe bound source cardinality. None proves the required exact-support rational pair or its converse formula reconstruction.
body.consumer: Resolving the question turns qualitative mechanism and support knowledge into auditable identification or nonidentification certificates for latent causal graphs.
